many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only

# ARC horizontal-bar tail recoloring

Use this when demos show a mostly uniform background, horizontal rows/bands of a second color, and output introduces color 1 in a background-colored trailing region or a marked endpoint.

## Evidence from a recurring task family

Observed demos had different palettes and sizes, but a common behavior: preserve the pattern and recolor the special right-side/background tail associated with the horizontal motif to 1.

- In a 10x28 demo, a row of 5s had a terminal 3 in the far-right cell; output changed that single terminal cell to 1, leaving other rows unchanged.
- In a 23x10 demo, one 7-pattern row ended in background 8; output changed only that far-right endpoint to 1. Similar-looking rows without a trailing background endpoint stayed unchanged.
- In a larger tiled demo, the matching rows had a three-cell trailing region at the right, changed from 8 to 1.
- In a sparse 29x27 test, the intended transformation was to recolor the complete trailing 9-region to the right of the short 7-bar on row 22 (1-indexed), not just the first cell after the bar. Other rows stayed as input.

## Method

1. Identify the background, horizontal motif color, and rows with a relevant horizontal bar/pattern.
2. Compare demos for the exact endpoint/tail condition. A uniquely marked terminal cell or repeated-width trailing patch may indicate the span to recolor.
3. In the test, recolor only the supported trailing background span to 1; preserve all other cells and dimensions.
4. Verify row and column counts before submitting. ARC inputs are conventionally described as height x width; count the actual row entries carefully, especially where a bar is cut short.
5. Do not assume the fill is one cell: demos can indicate a full contiguous tail (e.g. multiple trailing columns). Conversely, don't recolor other bars merely because they share the motif color.

Treat this as an evidence-based pattern, not a universal rule: request another demo when the tail span or row selection cannot be distinguished confidently, rather than extrapolating from color alone.",

# Horizontal bar with trailing tail recoloring

Use when demos show a mostly uniform background, horizontal rows/bands of a second color, and output introduces color 1 in a background-colored trailing region or marked endpoint.

## Evidence from this task family

Observed demos had different palettes and sizes, but common behavior: preserve the pattern and recolor the special right-side/background tail associated with the horizontal motif to 1.

- A 10x28 demo: a row of 5s had a terminal 3 in the far-right cell; output changed only that cell to 1.
- A 23x10 demo: a patterned row ended in background 8; output changed only that far-right endpoint to 1. Similar rows without that endpoint condition stayed unchanged.
- A tiled demo: matching rows had a three-cell trailing region at the right, changed from 8 to 1.
- A sparse 29x27 test: intended transformation was to recolor the full trailing 9-region to the right of the short 7-bar on row 22 (1-indexed), not just its first cell. Other rows stayed unchanged.

## Method

1. Identify background, horizontal motif color, and rows with the relevant bar/pattern.
2. Compare demos for the exact endpoint/tail condition. A terminal marker or repeated-width trailing patch may indicate span to recolor.
3. In test, recolor only the supported trailing background span to 1; preserve all other cells and dimensions.
4. Verify row and column counts before submitting. ARC dimensions are height x width; count actual row entries, especially where a bar is cut short.
5. Don't assume the fill is one cell: demos can indicate a multi-column contiguous tail. Don't recolor other bars merely because they share motif color.

This is evidence-based, not universal. Request another demo when tail span or row selection is ambiguous rather than extrapolating from color alone.",
